# Candidate application sentences (MIT Solve 2027)

<!-- Generated by research/solve2027-impact/compute.py from NUMBERS.json; do not edit by hand. -->

Each sentence and its caution are rendered from [`NUMBERS.json`](NUMBERS.json); the keys they rely on follow. Every number is model-relative: it describes what the Route-Check API concluded for recorded fire-scenario members of the March 2025 fires, not what happened to residents, and never an evacuation outcome or casualties avoided. Say "checked route (within the model)", never "safe route". Definitions and caveats: [README.md](README.md).

## S1

> Using the recorded March 2025 forecasts of the Uiseong-Andong and Yeongdeok wildfires, our planner checked vehicle departures for 174 OpenStreetMap-mapped villages and care facilities against 4 fire scenarios from the forecast, at six departure times 10 minutes apart after each of three recorded forecast times per region, in 9,396 recorded route checks (one per place, candidate destination and departure time).

NUMBERS.json keys: `places@all/places`, `attempts@all/pooled`, `records.route_checks@all/pooled`, `records.dispatch_attempts@all/pooled`, `records.rechecks@all/pooled`, `records.research_route_checks@all/pooled`, `osm_origins_not_checkable@all/places`, `cases@all/pooled`

Caution: Route checks are model computations by the Route-Check API recorded on the evaluated macOS host, not field trials or drills. The 4 fire scenarios are scenario members drawn independently per cell from the forecast, not simulations of the actual fire. The cache holds 9,722 route-check records in all: the 9,396 above, 279 re-checks of timed-out checks (shown in place of the original, as in the planner) and 47 checks of recorded research missions. 3 further OSM villages had no road node within 2 km and were never checked.

## S2

> In the recorded Uiseong-Andong scenarios, the share of villages and care facilities with a checked route (within the model) fell from 94.8% for departure at the forecast time to 40.9% for departure 50 minutes later (239 and 103 of 252 place-and-forecast-time cases).

NUMBERS.json keys: `cell.checked_route.offset_0000s@uiseong_andong_2025/pooled`, `cell.checked_route.offset_3000s@uiseong_andong_2025/pooled`, `places@uiseong_andong_2025/places`, `cell.checked_route.offset_0000s@yeongdeok_2025/pooled`, `cell.checked_route.offset_3000s@yeongdeok_2025/pooled`

Caution: Cases count each place once per recorded forecast time (84 places x 3). A departure without a checked route means the model found no route satisfying its checks for those scenario members, or could not judge; it is not a prediction that residents could not escape. In Yeongdeok the same share went from 97.0% to 93.0%; quote both regions together to avoid cherry-picking.

## S3

> In 21 of 522 place-and-forecast-time cases (4.0%), the model found no checked route at any of the six departure times: 11 had no route within the model and 10 were unresolved, which the planner never presents as safe.

NUMBERS.json keys: `no_checked_route_any_offset@all/pooled`, `best_verdict.model_no_route@all/pooled`, `best_verdict.unresolved@all/pooled`, `attempts.unresolved.AT_ISSUE_FAILURE@all/pooled`, `attempts.unresolved.TIMEOUT@all/pooled`, `places.no_checked_route_any_offset_any_input@all/places`, `no_checked_route_at_offset_0000s@all/pooled`, `deadline.none_model_no_route@all/pooled`, `deadline.none_unresolved@all/pooled`

Caution: "No route within the model" (model_no_route) is a statement about this model and input scope, not proof that escape is impossible. "Unresolved" means the system could not judge and must never be read as safe or as no-route; of all 9,396 displayed attempts, 186 were unresolved with API reason code AT_ISSUE_FAILURE ("limits already exceeded at departure") and 6 with TIMEOUT. These cases involve 21 distinct places; they are also exactly the 21 cases without a checked route for immediate departure.

## S4

> Counting each place once, 65 of 174 villages and care facilities (37.4%) had no checked route for a departure 50 minutes after the forecast time in at least one of the three recorded forecast times: their leave-by time in the planner was +40 minutes or earlier, or no checked route existed.

NUMBERS.json keys: `places.not_checked_at_offset_3000s_any_input@all/places`, `places.window_closes_within_hour_any_input@all/places`, `places.no_checked_route_any_offset_any_input@all/places`

Caution: Model-relative and tied to the recorded scenarios, the 10-minute departure grid and the 1-hour horizon. Of these places, 53 had a checked departure window that closed inside the hour and 21 had no checked route in some forecast time (a place can be in both). A place outside this count is not "safe": the scenario window simply ends at +50 minutes.

## S5

> At each place's leave-by time, the travel-time-only route to the same destination met predicted flames in at least one of 4 fire scenarios in 9 of 501 comparisons (1.8%, all in Uiseong-Andong); there the checked alternative took 0.5 to 21.8 minutes longer (median 5.5 minutes) and was 0.3 to 12.8 km longer.

NUMBERS.json keys: `travel_only.fastest_meets_flames@all/pooled`, `travel_only.extra_arrival_s.min@all/pooled`, `travel_only.extra_arrival_s.max@all/pooled`, `travel_only.extra_arrival_s.median@all/pooled`, `travel_only.extra_length_m.min@all/pooled`, `travel_only.extra_length_m.max@all/pooled`, `travel_only.clear_pairs_equal_arrival@all/pooled`, `travel_only.fastest_meets_flames@uiseong_andong_2025/pooled`

Caution: Only 9 comparisons; do not generalise. The comparison exists only at each place's latest checked departure and toward its default checked destination. "Predicted flames" = centre-model flame contact in at least one scenario member, not an observed fire. In the other 492 comparisons the fastest route had no predicted flame contact and arrived at the same second as the checked route (492 of 492). Never describe the checked route as "safe".

## S6

> On the road graph used for routing, every route from 115 of 174 villages and care facilities (66.1%) to their three candidate destinations shares at least one road segment, a single point of failure in the model's road network; for 108 of these it is the first segment leaving the place's road entry point.

NUMBERS.json keys: `redundancy.turn_aware_paths_1@all/places`, `redundancy.single_cut_at_entry_node@all/places`, `redundancy.turn_aware_equals_plain@all/places`, `destinations_used.school@all/places`, `destinations_used.community_hall@all/places`, `destinations_used.shelter@all/places`, `redundancy.entry_out_degree_1@all/places`

Caution: A property of the provisional pre-fire OSM road graph (2025-03-21 snapshot; missing one-way tags assumed two-way) and of the planner's entry point (nearest road node to the OSM point), not a field-verified count of access roads. "Shares at least one road segment" = the largest set of routes that pairwise share no directed road segment has one route (unit-capacity max-flow = 1, computed with and without turn restrictions, equal for 174 of 174 places); it ignores road capacity, travel time and fire. Candidate destinations are 68 OSM schools, 115 community halls and 1 OSM-mapped shelter, not official evacuation shelters.

## S7

> Every leave-by time in this analysis is reproducible: applying the planner's rules to the original attempts recorded by the Route-Check API reproduces the API's own deadline fields for 522 of 522 place-and-forecast-time cases, all 8 displayed differences are explained by re-checks of timed-out checks, and an independent second implementation recomputes every reported number.

NUMBERS.json keys: `api_check.recorded_equals_planner_rule_on_original@all/pooled`, `api_check.displayed_differs_explained_by_recheck@all/pooled`, `api_check.displayed_equals_recorded.latest_checked_depart_offset_s@all/pooled`

Caution: This is internal consistency of software and recorded data. It does not validate the forecast, the hazard model, the road data or real-world safety. The planner displays re-checks, so its deadline equals the API's recorded latest_checked_depart_offset_s for 517 of 522 cases.
